Keel: straight leading edge produced to the hull 5.35 m aft of the stem (its fillet meets the hull at 5.12), trailing edge 6.14; chord 0.79 m at the hull and 0.655 at the bulb; leading-edge sweep 15.8°; hull to bulb top 1.63 m, to keel bottom 2.23; bulb 1.77 m long, trailing aft of the fin. published.estimatedWhy: BWL is solved from ORC's sink; Tc, the keel, the bulb's length and the rudder are read off the designer's profile. The bulb's width is not published: its diameter is that of a spheroid of the drawn length holding 2,000 kg of lead (the profile's depth is 0.58 m). The model centres a bulb under the tip's quarter chord; the real one trails aft, its nose flush with the fin's leading edge, so the model's bulb sits about 0.7 m too far forward. The synthetic hull puts the waterline's forward end 0.6·(LOA − LWL) = 1.00 m aft of the stem; the drawing's is 0.50 m.
